protections: Login target validation: the `next` value is urlparse'd and redirected only if there is no netloc and the parsed path is under base_url, with an absolute URL allowed only when it matches a configured CORS origin or pattern (notebook/auth/login.py:42-59).

Constructed redirect targets: file, tree and deprecated-API redirects build their Location from base_url plus url_escape(path)/url_path_join instead of copying request data (notebook/base/handlers.py:874-900; notebook/tree/handlers.py:61-65; notebook/services/contents/handlers.py:294-298).
Startup rebasing of the operator default_url so that it starts with base_url before it is mounted as the `/` redirect (notebook/notebookapp.py:1393-1395).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The A fix already parses the target and rejects anything with a netloc, so a value whose parsed path starts with base_url looks like an in-tree link; the check reasons about the parsed path while the browser resolves the raw string, and a leading '///' (or a leading slash followed by a backslash) has an empty netloc yet still resolves to an authority when base_url is '/'.

request.uri is the origin-form request target, which is expected to start with '/', and the handler only strips a trailing slash; the change looks like cosmetic normalisation, it is far from the login redirect the report names, and the route is unauthenticated so it does not look like part of the redirect-trust path.

default_url is an operator-only traitlets setting rather than request data, and the startup check appears to keep it under base_url, so there is no attacker-controlled value and the redirect looks like configuration rather than a vulnerability.

masking: T2 -> T1: if the trailing-slash route were instead made to require login rather than validate its own target, the same '//host/' request target would become the login `next` value and T1's guard would be the only check deciding the redirect.

conflicts.what: Reusing the login guard unchanged for the trailing-slash route is wrong when allow_origin is configured: _redirect_safe deliberately allows full-domain redirects to a CORS-allowed origin (notebook/auth/login.py:47-54), a must-keep-working behaviour for T1, while the trailing-slash route has no reason to ever leave the origin; a shared validator must keep that exception scoped to the login route.

The natural T3 fix, normalising default_url at startup with url_path_join (notebookapp.py:1394-1395), changes the stored value that notebookapp.py:1740 slices by base_url for the browser-open file, so the same fix site must keep that slicing contract while dropping the scheme-relative form.

fairness_risks: Refusing any target that contains '//' would break the existing must-keep-working login cases with doubled slashes inside the path (notebook/auth/tests/test_login.py:39-48, e.g. 'tree//something'); only a leading scheme-relative form may be refused.

A strict same-origin-only rule for the login target contradicts the documented and implemented allow_origin full-domain redirect (notebook/auth/login.py:34-38, 47-54); CORS-allowed absolute redirects must keep working.
The trailing-slash redirect must keep working for ordinary directory URLs and preserve the query string, because it copies request.uri rather than request.path (notebook/base/handlers.py:865).

default_url must keep accepting ordinary in-tree values such as '/tree' and stay rebased under base_url (notebook/notebookapp.py:1393-1395); legitimate default_url values that begin with a single slash must not be refused by a leading-'//' rule.

Refused input shape that a legitimate use also needs: login `next` values that are base_url paths containing internal doubled slashes (notebook/auth/tests/test_login.py:44) and same-origin absolute URLs that match allow_origin.

design.why: T1 alone is a single judgement; the three traps need three different fix sites with three different dismissal arguments. T1 is the published incomplete-fix gap and the mimo-type judgement (a urlparse path check that mishandles the browser-resolved shape, coupled to allow_origin and to internal '//' paths). T2 is a real unauthenticated redirect route in the same package where no target validation ever existed, with the classic deepseek dismissal that request.uri is origin-form. T3 is a stored-config redirect whose startswith(base_url) rebase has the same leading-'//' blind spot, with an operator-config dismissal. Alternative designs lose independence: several login-target shapes collapse into one guard, and the constructed file/tree/API redirect sites add no real gap because url_path_join plus url_escape already constrain them to the origin.

unverified: The b_fix commit 979e0bd15e79 and the A-fix diffs could not be read from the pinned worktree (no git CLI in this session; only the pinned tree was in scope), so which exact guard the reference fix adds (leading-'//' only, or also backslash and cross-scheme forms) is unverified.
Whether any later upstream commit fixes the TrailingSlashHandler redirect, which would make T2 cleanly 'uncovered_upstream' rather than a designer-added trap, could not be checked.

The B advisory text and any proof-of-concept, and the hidden-test inputs, were not available; the leading-'///' shape is inferred from the pinned check plus browser URL resolution rules, not read from the advisory.
TrailingSlashHandler exploitability for a '//host/' request target was reasoned from Tornado's origin-form request handling and browser URL parsing; no runtime test was executed.
